_metadata.artifact_kind_note: This is a hand-authored seed artifact produced for the no-network-access, no-Linear-key analysis sandbox. The slas[] array is intentionally empty because (a) scripts/08_extract_linear.py cannot reach https://api.linear.app/graphql without LINEAR_API_KEY being set in the environment, and (b) a HEAD-scan of the repository's documentation tree (docs/, blitzy-docs/, blitzy/documentation/, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, README.md) discovered no SLA policy document defining defect resolution targets per severity tier. When the script is re-run with LINEAR_API_KEY set and network reachable, OR when an SLA policy document is added to the repository, the slas[] array is repopulated by the extraction script and this artifact is overwritten; the run_id and extraction_timestamp will then reflect that execution. The linear.* and repo_policy_scan.* sub-objects below document the queries and search commands that were attempted so that the Reproducibility Appendix in acceleration-report.md is complete even when no SLA source was reachable.

linear.unavailable_reason: LINEAR_API_KEY environment variable is not set; Linear API access is required to retrieve SLA targets for the Linear workspace referenced in the repository's PR and issue templates
linear.unavailable_reason_detail: The read-only analysis sandbox does not have a Linear API key configured. Per AAP §0.5.3.13, when no Linear API key is supplied, scripts/08_extract_linear.py exits the SLA-retrieval branch without issuing any HTTP request (per AAP §0.8.2 'No external system writes' and the no-secret-material-in-artifacts constraint) and falls back to the repository policy scan documented under repo_policy_scan below. The Linear API rejects all unauthenticated requests, so no anonymous SLA listing endpoint exists to query.
linear.auth_required: LINEAR_API_KEY environment variable (Linear personal API key or OAuth token with read scope on the workspace SLAs and issues).
linear.graphql_query_template: query SLAs { slaTargets { id name priority targetDuration } }
linear.graphql_query_template_note: This is the canonical GraphQL query that scripts/08_extract_linear.py would POST to https://api.linear.app/graphql when LINEAR_API_KEY is set. It enumerates the workspace's SLA target definitions (one row per severity tier) with fields id (Linear node ID), name (display name of the tier, e.g., 'Sev-1', 'Sev-2'), priority (Linear's 0..4 priority value where 1 is Urgent, 2 is High, 3 is Medium, 4 is Low), and targetDuration (ISO-8601 duration string such as 'PT4H' or 'P1D' depending on the workspace's configuration). The query is recorded verbatim here so that a future analyst with API access can paste it directly into the Linear GraphQL playground at https://studio.apollographql.com/public/Linear-API/variant/current/explorer to reproduce the extraction step. The query is also referenced from the Reproducibility Appendix of acceleration-report.md.
linear.graphql_query_supplementary_notes: If the workspace uses Linear's Initiatives feature for incident SLAs rather than the slaTargets type, a secondary query would be issued: 'query InitiativeSLAs { initiatives { nodes { id name slaTargetDuration } } }'. The 08_extract_linear.py script attempts the primary slaTargets query first and only falls back to initiatives if the primary returns an empty nodes array. Both query variants are documented in the script's source for reproducibility.
linear.linear_workspace_inference_source: Inferred from .github/pull_request_template.md line 7, which links to https://linear.app/rudderstack/search. The Linear workspace slug in linear.app URLs is the path segment immediately after the host; here that segment is 'rudderstack'. This is the upstream RudderStack project's Linear workspace, inherited via the PR template. The actual workspace used by the Blitzy-Sandbox/blitzy-RudderStack fork (if any) cannot be confirmed without API access, because the PR template is text-only and the Linear API key is required to enumerate workspace membership programmatically.
linear.consequence_for_metric_12: Without Linear API access, metrics.json#m12 (Defects Out of SLA) cannot use Linear's slaTargetDuration / slaBreachedAt fields as the primary SLA source. Per AAP §0.5.3.13, the metric falls back to a repository policy document scan; if that also fails (as documented in repo_policy_scan below), the metric reports 'insufficient_signal' with reason 'no SLA source'. The renderer in scripts/10_render_report.py propagates this reason verbatim into the Risk Assessment section of acceleration-report.md.

repo_policy_scan.search_command: grep -rniE 'SLA|severity|Sev-|priority response time|incident response' docs/ blitzy-docs/ blitzy/documentation/ CONTRIBUTING.md SECURITY.md README.md
repo_policy_scan.matches_found_definition_note: The 'matches_found: 0' value reports the count of matches that constitute an actual SLA POLICY document — that is, content defining a defect resolution target time bound to a severity tier (e.g., 'Sev-1 incidents must be resolved within 4 hours'). The literal regex grep command above returns a non-zero count of incidental keyword hits at HEAD, but every such hit is unrelated to defect SLA targets. The unrelated hits are catalogued in raw_keyword_hits_catalogue below so the search trail is fully transparent per Rule 1 (Data Provenance) and the no-fabrication constraint in AAP §0.7.3.

raw_keyword_hits_catalogue.raw_keyword_matches_command: grep -rniE 'SLA|severity|Sev-|priority response time|incident response' docs/ blitzy-docs/ blitzy/documentation/ CONTRIBUTING.md SECURITY.md README.md | wc -l

raw_match_categories_observed.description: Docs use the word 'severity' to rate the seriousness of a parity gap between this fork and upstream segment.com (e.g., 'Gap Severity: Medium', 'Critical severity'). These are product-feature gap classifications, not defect resolution SLAs.
The Warehouse service operates in master/slave mode; 'slave' substring matches the 'Sla' regex prefix under -i. These hits describe the operational mode of an in-process Go service, not a defect SLA.

The cloud source framework documentation tables include a 'Priority' column with values P0/P1/P2 that rank destination implementation priority for the engineering roadmap. These are product priority tags, not defect severity tiers.

Health monitoring documentation lists 'p95' (95th percentile latency) in JSON schema examples. The 'p1' / 'p95' substrings match P[0-9] patterns under refined searches but are observability metrics, not SLA targets.

Two documents reference 'SLA' in advice-form sentences without naming an SLA target value: docs/guides/transformations/user-transforms.md line 481 says 'Tune based on your SLA requirements' (parametric advice to operators); docs/guides/operations/privacy-compliance.md line 631 mentions 'faster deletion SLAs' as a tuning knob trade-off. Neither defines a numeric target for defect resolution.

docs/gap-report/sprint-roadmap.md lists task effort in days (e.g., '15 days', '8 days') in a sprint planning table. These are engineering effort estimates for upstream-parity work items, not defect resolution SLAs.

SECURITY.md contains the sentence 'We may fix the vulnerabilities in the older versions depending on the severity of the issue and the age of the release, but we are only committing to the latest version released.' This is a discretionary statement about supported versions, not a numeric SLA target tied to severity tiers.
CONTRIBUTING.md mentions 'Slack' (the messaging platform) several times in community-channel links; the 'Sla' substring matches case-insensitively. These are unrelated to SLAs.

raw_keyword_hits_catalogue.raw_keyword_hits_catalogue_note: Each category above was verified by manual inspection of the grep output at extraction time. None of the 166 raw matches is an SLA policy entry. Therefore matches_found (which counts SLA POLICY entries, not raw keyword hits) is correctly reported as 0.

supplementary_precision_search.command: grep -rniE '(P[0-3]|Sev-?[1-4]|critical|high|medium|low).*[0-9]+\s*(hour|day|minute|min|hr|d\b)' docs/ blitzy-docs/ blitzy/documentation/ CONTRIBUTING.md SECURITY.md README.md | grep -iE '(SLA|response|resolution|incident|target)'
supplementary_precision_search.command_purpose: A targeted second-pass search looking for the canonical SLA policy pattern: severity tier (P0..P3 or Sev-1..Sev-4 or critical/high/medium/low) co-located with a numeric duration (hours/days/minutes) and an SLA-context keyword (response/resolution/incident/target).
supplementary_precision_search.supplementary_note: Three hits were initially returned, all from docs/gap-report/sprint-roadmap.md: (i) line 448 '15 days' is a sprint effort estimate for E-026 (identity graph implementation); (ii) line 543 '8 days' is a sprint effort estimate for E-037 with a mention that the warehouse-sync application should alert when latency exceeds the user's configured SLA — a product feature, not a defect SLA; (iii) line 763 'P2' in a sprint roadmap table refers to product implementation priority, not defect severity. None constitutes an SLA policy entry, so the canonical matches_found stays at 0.

repo_policy_scan.conclusion: No SLA policy document discovered in repository; the PR template (.github/pull_request_template.md) and issue template (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug-report.md) confirm Linear as the external tracker for code changes, but the SLA targets live in Linear (which is unavailable in this run because LINEAR_API_KEY is not set). The 166 raw keyword hits are all incidental matches (parity-gap severity ratings, master/slave architecture mode, destination priority tags, p95 latency metrics, sprint effort estimates, and one discretionary clause in SECURITY.md about version support); the supplementary precision search confirms zero severity-tier-to-duration mappings exist anywhere in the documentation tree.

unavailable_reason_detail: Neither of the two SLA sources defined by AAP §0.5.3.13 yielded a result: (1) the Linear API is unreachable because LINEAR_API_KEY is not set in the analysis environment, and (2) the repository documentation tree contains no SLA policy document defining defect resolution targets per severity tier. Per AAP §0.5.3.13 and §0.7.3 (no fabrication), the platform reports this metric as 'insufficient_signal' rather than inventing targets.

summary.primary_source_status_detail: LINEAR_API_KEY environment variable is not set; no HTTP request was issued to https://api.linear.app/graphql.
summary.fallback_source_status_detail: Repository policy scan executed over six documented paths (docs/, blitzy-docs/, blitzy/documentation/, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, README.md) using the 14-keyword search list; 166 raw regex hits were observed and inspected, none of which is an SLA policy entry (full category breakdown in repo_policy_scan.raw_keyword_hits_catalogue).
summary.downstream_metric_impact: metrics.json#m12 (Defects Out of SLA) must be reported as 'insufficient_signal' with reason 'no SLA source'. The Risk Assessment section of acceleration-report.md must include a row for m12 explaining that without either Linear API access or a repository SLA policy document, no defect-resolution SLA target exists against which to measure defect closures.

to_populate_via_linear_api: 1. Obtain a Linear personal API key from https://linear.app/settings/api with read scope on issues, labels, and SLAs.
2. Export the key into the analysis environment: 'export LINEAR_API_KEY=lin_api_xxx'.
3. Re-run the extraction step: 'cd blitzy/acceleration-report && . .venv/bin/activate && python scripts/08_extract_linear.py'.
4. The script will overwrite this artifact with the populated slas[] array sourced from Linear's slaTargets type, and the linear.available field will be set to true.
5. Re-run the compute step: 'python scripts/09_compute_metrics.py' to derive metrics.json#m12 from the populated slas[] array.
to_populate_via_repo_policy_document: 1. Author a Markdown policy document at one of the searched paths (e.g., docs/policies/defect-resolution-sla.md) with a table mapping severity tiers (P0..P3 or Sev-1..Sev-4) to target resolution durations (in hours or days).

2. Commit the document to the analyzed repository (subject to its standard PR workflow; this step is outside the scope of the read-only acceleration-report platform and must be performed by a repository maintainer).
3. Re-run the extraction step: 'python scripts/08_extract_linear.py' — the repo_policy_scan branch will discover the new document, parse it, and populate slas[] with source: 'repo_policy' entries.
4. Re-run the compute step to derive metrics.json#m12 from the policy-document SLA targets.
rerun_instructions.rerun_instructions_note: Both branches above are documented in the Reproducibility Appendix of acceleration-report.md (per AAP Rule 5: Reproducibility) and in blitzy/acceleration-report/onboarding/rerun-and-observability.md (per AAP §0.7.1.2: Onboarding & Continued Development).

per_sla_schema_when_populated.schema_note: When the slas[] array is non-empty (after a successful Linear API extraction or after a policy document is added to the repo), each entry MUST follow the schema below. This schema is reproduced here for documentation completeness so that a future analyst can validate populated entries without consulting external documentation.

required_fields.severity: string; the severity tier label as defined by the source (e.g., 'P0', 'P1', 'P2', 'P3', 'Sev-1', 'critical', 'high', 'medium', 'low')
required_fields.target_duration_iso8601: string; the SLA target duration as an ISO-8601 duration string (e.g., 'PT4H' for 4 hours, 'P1D' for 1 day, 'PT30M' for 30 minutes)
required_fields.target_duration_seconds: integer; the SLA target duration converted to seconds for arithmetic comparisons in the compute step
required_fields.source_locator: string; a URL path (for linear_api source) such as 'https://linear.app/<workspace>/settings/sla/<id>', or a file path with line locator (for repo_policy source) such as 'docs/policies/defect-resolution-sla.md:L14'

per_sla_schema_when_populated.example_when_populated_note: The two example entries above are FOR SCHEMA DOCUMENTATION ONLY — they are illustrative ISO-8601 / seconds conversions, not actual SLA targets retrieved from any source. They MUST NOT be consumed by the compute step. The compute step reads slas[] (the empty array above), not per_sla_schema_when_populated.example_when_populated.
